drills.q: Analyst runs SELECT * on an unpartitioned 8TiB table 5 times. On-demand cost?
drills.a: ~40 TiB scanned = ~$250 (minus free tier). Fixes: partition+cluster, explicit columns, maximum_bytes_billed, dry-run discipline. LIMIT would not have helped.

drills.q: Estate scans 400 TiB/month with high scan-per-slot ratio. Which billing mode and why?
drills.a: Capacity: at that volume Enterprise PAYG 100-slot floor ($4,380/mo) buys ~701 TiB equivalent on-demand; if GiB/slot-hour ratio exceeds ~9.8 the slots are cheaper. Verify ratio from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS before committing.

drills.q: Moved to Enterprise Edition, bill rose 40%. Diagnose.
drills.a: Likely compute-heavy/scan-light workload (joins/aggregations on small tables) - few GiB per slot-hour means byte metering was cheaper. Fix: mixed assignments (reserve only scan-heavy projects), autoscaler baseline sizing, or revert mode.

drills.q: Duplicates appear in BigQuery from Pub/Sub pipeline. Explain and list fix tiers.
drills.a: At-least-once redelivery (ack deadline expiry, client restarts) is normal. Tiers: idempotent sink via message_id dedup; exactly-once subscriptions (pull-only, regional); BigQuery subscriptions writing once per message. Never trade duplicates for losses by retrying less.

drills.q: One device's telemetry must be processed strictly in order at high volume. Design.
drills.a: Ordering keys per-device for FIFO, accepting per-key throughput caps and availability cost; DLQ configured so a poison event can't block its key forever; consumers handle key-affinity shifts. If using Dataflow instead: rely on Beam windowing, not Pub/Sub keys.

drills.q: Dataflow watermark falls hours behind after a backfill starts. Debug sequence?
drills.a: Check backlog age metric; identify hot keys concentrating state (re-key/fan-out); check source quotas/backpressure; verify worker CPU and autoscaling bounds; confirm allowed lateness accommodates the burst rather than dropping data.

drills.q: Nightly PySpark job runs 2h/day on a persistent cluster. Redesign options ranked.
drills.a: 1) Dataproc Serverless batch (zero cluster mgmt). 2) Ephemeral cluster per run with Spot secondaries. Persistent only if interactive sessions share it - otherwise delete after each job.

drills.q: Poison messages never reach your DLQ despite config. Root cause?
drills.a: Pub/Sub service agent missing roles/pubsub.publisher on the DLQ topic - forwarding is best-effort and fails silently without IAM. Grant service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com and alert on dead_letter_message_count.

drills.q: Marketing asks why they should pay for Looker when Looker Studio is free.
drills.a: Looker sells governance: one governed definition per metric compiled to SQL, API access, central permissions, drilling/exploration. If metrics live consistently in dbt + modeled tables already, Studio achieves similar outcomes free - decide on definition-drift pain, not features.

drills.q: What breaks first at 10x volume across this stack? Rank with reasons.
drills.a: 1) Ordering keys (per-key serialization caps). 2) Dataflow hot keys (state concentration). 3) Slot contention under concurrent transforms (autoscaler absorbs if bounded). 4) Looker dashboards on raw detail tables (pre-aggregate). Serialization points fail before raw throughput limits.
